DECISION — keybinding scheme (Windows + Linux):
1. tmux keeps prefix Ctrl+Space. It must work in every host (WezTerm, Windows Terminal, VS Code, SSH); Ctrl+A conflicts with readline beginning-of-line, Ctrl+B with Claude Code's background key.
2. WezTerm leader moves Ctrl+Space -> Ctrl+Shift+Space. Same physical location (Shift added), free on Windows and Linux, and unlike Alt+Space it does not collide with the Windows window system menu.
3. Remove Ctrl+Shift+Q (QuitApplication) entirely: with window_close_confirmation=NeverPrompt a mistype kills every session.
4. Drop vim-tmux-navigator root-table C-h/j/k/l: restores Ctrl+L (shell clear AND Claude Code /clear); pane navigation remains prefix+h/j/k/l (tmux) and leader+h/j/k/l (WezTerm).
5. New: ScrollToPrompt(-1)/(1) on Ctrl+Shift+UpArrow/DownArrow in WezTerm (requires OSC 133 from term-crr.5).
6. Protected keys never bound at root tables anywhere: Ctrl+O, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+A/E (readline), Ctrl+Space (tmux prefix).

The generated wezterm.lua sets `config.default_prog = wsl_startup_args` globally on

becomes dead once the global assignment is gone.

The function has exactly two callers in the wheel - merge.py:695 inside _commit_tracker_state, which only fires when git status shows nothing but engine-tracker paths, and the broken advice string. basicly.toml declares no [tracker] section at all. config.py:838 states that until the cutover the prefix lived in .beads/config.yaml, and ours pins issue_prefix: term. tracker import preserved every term-* id verbatim but did not carry the prefix over and did not mention it. - wezterm.exe resolves to <redacted:windows-drive-path> Files\WezTerm\wezterm.exe — MACHINE scope, not user scope.
- Version is 20240203-110809-5046fc22. That is February 2024, about 2.5 years stale.
- winget list --id wez.wezterm confirms it is winget-managed at that version.
- There is NO user-local copy: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\WezTerm does not exist.

For contrast, the WSL wezterm is 20260707-093716-fff02ca5 — current. So the stale bundled Nerd Font is a Windows-only condition, which matches the original missing-glyph toast being Windows-only.

It found the Program Files one and left it alone. So no amount of re-running terminal-setup will refresh WezTerm on this machine.

WHAT THIS CHANGES: winget upgrade wez.wezterm against a machine-scope package needs elevation, so this is NOT a no-admin task as recorded. Two options for whoever picks it up, and they should be decided rather than defaulted:
(a) elevated winget upgrade wez.wezterm, keeping the machine-scope install; or
(b) winget uninstall then let terminal-setup install the portable user-scope copy to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs, which is the layout terminal-setup actually wants and would keep this no-admin from then on. Costs one PATH change and removes WezTerm for any other user of the box.

(b) is the one that matches this repo preference for no-admin user-local installs, but it is a machine-wide removal and is the owner call.

RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied.

WHAT HAPPENED. Running the four basicly projection gates, I set B="uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@v0.12.0 basicly" and then called "$B $g" in a loop. All four exited 127 with "no such file or directory: uvx --from ... basicly" - zsh expanded the whole string as a single command word rather than splitting it into argv. Nothing ran. Re-running the commands inline gave exit 0 on all four.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT CATCH IT. The non-interactive-shell fragment already warns about this class, but it names only the loop case: "Never loop over an unquoted variable (for x in $LIST): zsh does not word-split, so it runs once with the whole string and the silent no-op looks like success." I was not looping over a list. I was expanding a variable that held a multi-word COMMAND. Same mechanism, same silent-success failure mode, outside the stated scope - so the rule read as inapplicable.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. 127 is loud, so this one was caught immediately. The dangerous version is a variable holding a command whose first word IS a real binary: zsh passes the remaining words as one argument rather than failing, and the command runs with wrong arguments and exit 0. That is the shape the existing bullet already calls out for lists and is exactly as available here.

PROPOSED CHANGE, to the non-interactive-shell fragment. Widen the existing bullet from loops to any unquoted expansion of a variable holding more than one word, keeping the concrete zsh reason:

  Never expand an unquoted variable that holds multiple words - neither a list
  (for x in $LIST) nor a command (\$CMD arg). zsh does not word-split, so the
  whole string becomes one word: the loop runs once, or the command is not
  found (127) - or worse, runs with its arguments mangled into one and exits 0.
  Use an inline command, an array (for x in "${arr[@]}" / "${cmd[@]}"), or one
  batch command - then check the count actually changed.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: a hook that refuses unquoted $VAR in command position. Rejected as too broad - most unquoted expansions are single-word and correct, so it would fire constantly and get disabled, which is the failure mode a gate must avoid.

RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied. This is the finding that cost the most: a whole session was blocked overnight on a conclusion that was wrong.

WHAT HAPPENED. The prior session needed to scrub machine paths out of the imported ledger. The tracker-path-scan hook printed repair advice naming basicly.br.scrub_ledger. That import raises, so the session probed for the module - pkgutil over basicly.__path__ - found no br, and recorded: "the repair the hook prints CANNOT RUN: it names basicly.br.scrub_ledger, the real function is scrub_export, and the br module is not shipped in the wheel at all". The ledger migration was declared blocked on an upstream fix and left overnight.

Both halves were wrong. tracker.scrub_ledger ships in v0.12.0 at basicly/tracker.py:976 and works - it rewrote 92 of 141 events on first run. scrub_export does not exist anywhere in the wheel. One grep -rn "scrub" over the installed package - about ten seconds - would have found it immediately.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT CATCH IT. The external-facts fragment says: "An empty probe is not evidence of absence. A search returning nothing is ambiguous between absent and wrong probe... Run a positive control that must return something before you report a zero; if the control is empty too, the zero belongs to the probe."

That rule, followed exactly, would NOT have caught this. The probe was correct and its zero was true: there genuinely is no br module. A positive control for "does module br exist" would also have come back empty, and the rule would have confirmed the wrong conclusion rather than refusing it.

THE ACTUAL GAP. The probe asked about a LOCATION - does module X exist. The conclusion asserted a CAPABILITY - no consumer can scrub the ledger. Those are different claims, and a true answer to the first says nothing about the second. The existing rule guards against a bad probe; it does not guard against a good probe answering a different question than the one being reported.

PROPOSED CHANGE, to the external-facts fragment. Add one bullet beside the positive-control rule:

  **A capability is absent only when its VERB is absent, not its address.**
  "Module X does not exist" and "this cannot be done" are different claims;
  a true answer to the first is no evidence for the second, and a positive
  control cannot tell them apart because both come back empty. Before
  reporting a capability missing, grep the artifact for what the capability
  DOES - the verb, the effect - not the name you expected it under. A stale
  doc, a rename or a moved module all produce a true zero at the address and
  a live function one grep away.

WHY A RULE RATHER THAN A HABIT: the wrong conclusion was written into the tracker as settled fact, with evidence attached, and read by the next session as ground truth. It was only caught because that session happened to re-probe. Recorded confidence is what made this expensive, and nothing in the loop re-checks a recorded absence.

BRANCH NOT TAKEN: blaming the upstream advice string. The advice WAS wrong and is now fixed upstream, but that is a separate defect - the wrong name cost minutes, the wrong inference cost a session. Fixing only the advice would leave this class open.
payload.title: external-facts: absence of an address is not absence of a capability

RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Proposal only - not self-applied. This is a NEAR MISS, not a failure: the loss was caught one commit before it happened, and only because the owner had chosen to split the work.

WHAT ALMOST HAPPENED. The beads-to-ledger migration runbook ended with "retire .beads/". Every prior step had been verified - 49 of 50 records imported with ids preserved verbatim, comments and dependency edges intact, the one refusal a known tombstoned duplicate. By every check the runbook named, the cutover was complete and .beads/ was safe to delete.

It was not. The id prefix "term" lived in .beads/config.yaml as issue_prefix, and tracker import does not carry it - it preserves existing ids verbatim but writes no [tracker] prefix into basicly.toml. Reads, comments and updates all worked, so nothing surfaced it. Only minting a NEW root record was refused, and the session had not needed to mint one. Deleting .beads/ would have destroyed the only declaration of our own id namespace, and the discovery would have come weeks later when someone filed a record, with nothing left to recover the string from but git history.

It was caught because the owner had chosen to retire .beads/ in a separate commit after the release, which forced one more look at the directory. Had it been one commit, it would have shipped.

ROOT CAUSE. The verification asked "did everything transfer?" and the answer was yes. The question that needed asking was "what does the source hold that the target does not?" - a different question with a different answer. A migration checklist built from the importer output can only enumerate what the importer knows about; the prefix was invisible to it precisely because the importer never read it.

PROPOSED CHANGE. A bullet, best placed in the quality-gate fragment beside "exercise the change as it will really be used":

  **Before retiring a source system, enumerate what it holds that the target
  does NOT.** Reconciling what transferred only proves the transfer; it cannot
  see a thing the migration tool never read. List the source directory file by
  file and account for each one - config and metadata, not just the data
  export - because the file nobody migrated is the file nobody will miss until
  it is gone.

CONCRETE FORM IT WOULD HAVE TAKEN HERE: .beads/ held four tracked files. issues.jsonl was migrated. config.yaml held the prefix and was not. metadata.json and .gitignore were beads-runtime only and genuinely disposable. Four files, four answers - about two minutes, against a silent namespace loss.

BRANCH NOT TAKEN: treating this as an upstream bug only. It IS one, and basicly fixed it the same day (the import report now names the prefix). But their fix only speaks on a FRESH import, and ours ran under v0.12.0, so no report will ever print it for this repo. A consumer-side rule is what would have caught it here, and will catch the next migration whose tool has no such fix.

RETRO FINDING from the 2026-09-11 release session. Environment/tooling friction, filed as a quirk with its workaround.

WHAT HAPPENED. The session-finish skill opens its close-out ritual with "Report it with: basicly usage report". That command was refused by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier ("Blocked by classifier"), so the documented first step of the documented close-out cannot run. The same classifier refused winget upgrade --id wez.wezterm (reasonable - it can install) and, earlier and more consequentially, a raw python -c that rewrote the ledger in place.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS, and it is read-only: the counter the command formats is plain JSON at .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json, keyed by pipeline head with {count, last_used}. Reading and sorting it directly gives the same data. Skill invocations appear in the same file prefixed skill:, so both tables are recoverable.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BULLET RATHER THAN A SHRUG. A skill that instructs a blocked command trains the reader to treat the refusal as the anomaly and go looking for a way around it. That is the exact instinct that should NOT be encouraged - the classifier was right about the other two refusals, and the one that mattered (the in-place ledger rewrite) was right for precisely the reason that made it inconvenient: there was no named command for the operation, which is itself the defect. Upstream has since shipped basicly tracker scrub and it now runs unblocked, which is the correct resolution shape: when a sandbox blocks a repair, the fix is usually a named command, not an exemption.

PROPOSED CHANGE - one quirks bullet:

  `basicly usage report` is refused by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier.
  Read `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json` directly instead - same data, keyed by
  pipeline head, with `skill:` prefixed rows for skill invocations. More
  generally: when the sandbox blocks a repair, prefer asking for a named

payload.description:
The committed tracker log .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl is not declared '-text merge=union' anywhere, so two branches that both append events produce a same-line conflict git cannot auto-resolve.

EVIDENCE
  git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl
    -> text: auto
    -> eol: lf
  No merge driver. .gitattributes has no events- line at all; .git/info/attributes does not exist.

WHY IT IS REQUIRED
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/SPEC.md:185 says to declare 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union' in the deployment.
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py:95 says the kit "needs one line from its deployment that it cannot write itself", naming the same line.

ORIGIN
  Pre-existing. The basicly v0.12.1 install (commit a6b3f6d, the beads cutover) committed the log but never added the attributes line. This is a gap in our deployment, not a basicly v0.14.0 regression.

INTERACTION WITH basicly v0.14.0
  v0.14.0 shards writes to .basicly/ledger/pending-<branch>.jsonl and its install adds 'pending-*.jsonl -text merge=union'. If install writes only the pending- line and assumes the events- line already exists, the trunk log is still unprotected after the upgrade. Confirm which lines install actually writes.

FIX
  Add 'events-*.jsonl -text merge=union' to .gitattributes, alongside whatever pending- line install adds. Needs owner confirmation: .gitattributes is on the confirmation list.
payload.title: Ledger log has no union merge driver: .gitattributes is missing the events-*.jsonl line

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given the terminal repo at HEAD, when 'git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl' is run, then it reports 'merge: union' in addition to text/eol. Positive control: the same command on a file matching no rule reports no merge attribute, proving the probe distinguishes the two.

payload.description:
basicly v0.14.0's ENGINE install path writes only the events-*.jsonl merge rule to .gitattributes. It never writes the pending-*.jsonl rule, although the standalone kit installer does and the docs promise both.

EVIDENCE, all at tag v0.14.0 = 75e3b03ed03e254d81ace31e72b18b0f9fba5cd1

  src/basicly/cli.py:1407 -> _scaffold_ledger_attributes(repo_root)
  src/basicly/cli.py:1182-1201  writes exactly the rules returned by owned_write.ledger_git_rules
  src/basicly/owned_write.py:25-30
      def ledger_git_rules(repo_root) -> tuple[str, ...]:
          log_glob = owned_store.kit(repo_root, "events").LOG_GLOB
          return (f"{log_glob} -text merge=union",)          # events only, no pending
  Upstream's own test pins this: tests/test_install_ledger_attributes.py asserts
      owned_write.ledger_git_rules(work_repo) == (RULE,)   with RULE = "events-*.jsonl -text merge=union"
  No pending- attribute rule is written anywhere in cli.py. The only pending- mention in that file is
  cli.py:1698, which globs both names for a presence check, not for attributes.

WHAT DOES WRITE BOTH (the other path, not the one we use)
  packages/basicly-tracker/basicly_tracker/__init__.py
      (".gitattributes", tuple(f"{glob} -text merge=union" for glob in (log_glob, pending_glob)))
  docs/reference/kits.md says ".gitattributes gains events-*.jsonl and pending-*.jsonl, each -text merge=union"

WHY IT BITES THIS REPO SPECIFICALLY
  The shard name derives from .git/HEAD, so it is per-BRANCH, not per-writer. terminal is worked on from
  two machines and both sit on main, so both produce the identical path .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl.
  Two appends to the same tracked file with no merge=union is the exact same-line conflict the union rule
  exists to prevent - the failure the ledger design is built to escape. The per-branch shard only separates
  writers when the branches differ.
  Secondary: with no -text, terminal's blanket "* text=auto eol=lf" rule in .gitattributes applies to the
  shards, which the kit deliberately disables for the trunk log.

REPRODUCE
  Run `basicly install` from v0.14.0, then:
    git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl     # expect: no merge attribute
    git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl      # expect: merge: union   (positive control)
  The second line is the control: it must show the rule, proving the probe reads attributes correctly and
  the first result is a real absence rather than a bad query.

NOT YET OBSERVED
  Filed from source reading at the tag, not from a completed install - the upgrade is on hold pending the
  owner's go-ahead and upstream quality-gates. Confirm both check-attr lines after installing.

REPORTED UPSTREAM
  Yes, to the basicly session. Their briefing stated install adds the pending- rule; for the engine path it
  does not. Fix belongs in basicly (ledger_git_rules and its test), not here.
